title: The Importance Of The Bathroom In Winning Residential Design
bodyHtml:
Why is the Bathroom so important from a Buyer's Perspective?

Property is a complex beast – no more is it as simple as ‘location, location, locaation’. Of course, location is right up there when buyers are making real estate decisions, as are amenities. But thanks to the proliferation of real estate-related media, including the ubiquitous reality television show, the mainstream buyer is now more aware than ever of the value of design.

“To some buyers today, quality design is as important as the location and amenities,“ says George Banjanin, Senior Development Manager at Loftex Property, who specialise in the development of high quality residential apartments. 

Group GSA, photography by Tyrone Branigan

The kitchen has long been recognised as the most important room in the home when it comes to the sell pitch. Following closely – and often the smallest room in the house – is the bathroom. Banjanin details how crucial this space is, in his experience. “The quality of the bathroom reflects on the quality of the rest of the development,” he says. “That starts with the bathrooms that we show in our display apartments. We always feature an accurate display bathroom so that a potential purchaser can imagine the space in their finished apartment.” 

Brendan Fearn of Bresic Whitney agrees that this room needs to be carefully considered by the seller. “It is better to have a totally unrenovated bathroom than a renovated bathroom that a buyer will feel they need to renovate again,” he says. “It's integral that a seller renovates a bathroom,” he continues, “not to please themselves, but rather to please the market. And that means not just white.... but [a design that is] up-to-date with the current trend."

SJB Interiors and SJB Architects, image courtesy of Evolve

Banjanin says that the most important aspects to consider are the longevity of the product –whether the modern finishes will visually look as impressive in 5 or 10 years as they do today, as well as ensuring the durability of the fittings and accessories. In terms of what product is the absolute most important within the bathroom, Fearn votes for “Baths by a long way – every house should have one bath. Second is a walk-in shower with rain head”.
